brief: A portable electronics organizer: a base with removable bins for small parts, at least one drawer, and a carry handle.

requirements.requirement: Portable electronics organizer with a base
requirements.evidence: Four level-0 bases (piece:0,0,0;full, piece:1,0,0;full, piece:1,-1,0;full, piece:0,1,0;half-n) locked together with joint bolts and capped open faces, forming one group per check_build.

Three drop-in removable bins: bin:0,0,0~hex-bin-full-div3 (3 compartments), bin:1,0,0~hex-bin-full-div2 (2 compartments), bin:1,-1,0~hex-bin-full (open), dressed with M3 screw/nut/standoff heaps visible from above.
drawer:0#0,1#cut fitted on the cut face of the half-n base at 0,1,0, with a top cover over it.
handle:1,-1,0;top mounted on top cover cover:1,-1,0;full;top at the corner of the cluster.

finish.summary: Built a portable electronics organizer: 4 hex bases at level 0 (three full, one half-n) joined and locked, three removable drop-in bins (div3, div2, and open full-depth) filled with M3 screws, nuts and standoffs, one drawer on the half-base cut face, and a chain carry handle on a top cover. House rules applied (capOpenFaces, lockJoints); check_build is clear with no issues.

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
